- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns positive (≥0.3) mid-period, model frequently fails to fully capture momentum; increase forecast slope or add 1–2% lagged momentum bias.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when price deviates >3σ from 14-day moving average; apply correction toward historical mean if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.3), model overfits short-term noise; use 5-day smoothing filter on forecast to reduce false peaks.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3 consecutive days, model is underestimating upward momentum; add 0.5–1% daily bias to next forecast if sentiment remains bullish.
